# PortableMind

> The AI-native workspace — team memory, agents, files, tasks and conversations — exposed to any AI app as an MCP server. Endpoint: https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp

## Connecting
- [Connecting an agent to PortableMind (MCP)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/connect.md): Endpoint, authentication, workspace scoping, tool filtering and response shape for the PortableMind MCP server.
- [Recipes: what agents get wrong, and the right call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/recipes.md): Short, correct call shapes for the PortableMind MCP tools that are most often misused. Each recipe is also a Context7 rule.

- [conversation_chat_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/conversation_chat_tool.md): Send a chat message directly to an LLM conversation.

- [read_llm_file_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/read_llm_file_tool.md): Read the contents of an existing LlmFile by ID.
- [remote_directory_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/remote_directory_tool.md): List directory contents on a remote code workspace via SSH.
- [remote_file_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/remote_file_tool.md): Read, write, patch, or delete files on a remote code workspace via SSH.
- [remote_git_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/remote_git_tool.md): Perform git operations on a remote code workspace via SSH.
- [remote_search_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/remote_search_tool.md): Search code on a remote workspace via SSH using ripgrep (rg) or grep.
- [remote_shell_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/remote_shell_tool.md): Run allowlisted shell commands on a remote code workspace via SSH.
- [reply_to_customer_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/reply_to_customer_tool.md): Reply to the CUSTOMER on a support ticket.
- [report_coding_session_usage_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/report_coding_session_usage_tool.md): Report the token usage of a coding-agent CLI session you ran (Claude Code, Gemini, or Codex) so its cost is tracked under your user.
- [run_python_skill_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/run_python_skill_tool.md): Run an approved, server-side Python skill by name and (if it generates a file) attach the result to the conversation.
- [search_conversation_history_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/search_conversation_history_tool.md): Search the message history of a conversation for a keyword or phrase.
- [send_conversation_invitation_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/send_conversation_invitation_tool.md): Send an email invitation to a user to join and respond to an LLM conversation.
- [send_email_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/send_email_tool.md): Send an email based on a email body, subject, sender and reciever make sure to send all required fields, email_body can not be empty.
- [send_guest_invitation_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/send_guest_invitation_tool.md): Send a guest invitation email to join an LLM conversation.
- [set_agent_state_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/set_agent_state_tool.md): Flip a state flag on your own custom_fields.
- [show_user_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/show_user_tool.md): Point out a UI element to the user with an on-screen callout ("show me where X is", "where do I…", "how do I find…").
- [silolink_session_control_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/silolink_session_control_tool.md): Inspect or control an existing SiloLink (Claude Code) session.
- [start_dm_with_user_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/start_dm_with_user_tool.md): Open a direct-message conversation with another user/agent in the same tenant and post an opening message.
- [store_memory_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/store_memory_tool.md): Store persistent memories for future AI sessions.
- [test_llm_tool_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/test_llm_tool_tool.md): Test execute a custom LLM Tool with provided parameters.
- [update_agent_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/update_agent_tool.md): Update an existing LLM agent by name.
- [update_llm_file_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/update_llm_file_tool.md): Update existing LlmFile records with new content, title, or directory location.
- [update_memory_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/update_memory_tool.md): Correct or refine an existing memory you own (title / content / importance / tags).

- [validate_rich_content_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/validate_rich_content_tool.md): Validate a chart or card before you post it.
- [walk_user_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/walk_user_tool.md): Walk the user through a MULTI-STEP task with guided on-screen callouts.
- [web_research_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/web_research_tool.md): Web research tool for researcher agents.
- [worker_completion_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/worker_completion_tool.md): Signal that your dispatched work is COMPLETE.

- [workspace_provision_tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/mcp/tools/workspace_provision_tool.md): Self-provision a development workspace for an agent.

## User guides
- [PortableMind user guides](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/README.md): The in-app guides from https://www.portablemind.ai/docs, in reading order. For the MCP tool reference see [https://github.com/portablemind-ai/docs/blob/main/mcp/README.md](https://github.com/portablemind-ai/docs/blob/main/mcp/README.md).
- [Building AI Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/agents.md): **Tip:** Use manual execution with different role combinations to see how your agent behaves in different contexts. A content agent run with only its "Technical Writer" role selected might focus on documentation; adding "Marketing Specialist" makes it more promotional. Combine that with a one-off instruction like "focus on API endpoints" to steer a single run precisely.
- [Chat & the AI Assistant](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/ai-assistant.md): **Tip:** In long-running conversations, `/compact` keeps responses fast and focused by summarizing earlier history instead of resending all of it.
- [Setting Up AI Models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/ai-setup.md): **Note:** AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI work differently from the rest. Instead of a per-model API key, each uses a single workspace-level connection to your cloud account, shared by every model it serves. They have their own setup guides — [Bedrock](bedrock-setup.md) and [Vertex](vertex-setup.md) — and the rest of this page does not apply to them.
- [Connecting AWS Bedrock](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/bedrock-setup.md): **Note:** Brand-new AWS accounts are sometimes gated for a day or so even after model access is granted, returning a 403 that says the model "is not available for this account". This usually clears itself within 24 hours — it is not a configuration error on your side.
- [Coding Agents (SiloLink)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/coding-agents.md): **Note:** Token usage for all three agents is captured automatically and rolled up under your user in AI Studio's cost analysis — see [Cost tracking](#cost-tracking) below.
- [Communications Hub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/communications-hub.md): **Note:** **Multi-tenant by design.** Each tenant gets their own isolated channel instances with their own credentials. A single Hub deployment serves all tenants securely — your channels, credentials, and messages are never visible to any other tenant.
- [Custom Data: Levels & Tiers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/custom-data-tiers.md): "Create a custom object type called Engine with torque in Nm, max RPM, and fuel type (petrol or diesel). Then add the M20B25: 222 Nm, 6500 RPM, petrol."
- [Developer Resources](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/developers.md): **Tip:** If you're building AI agents that act on the platform, start with the MCP tools reference — it's usually a faster path than the raw REST API.
- [Dynamic Functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/dynamic-functions.md): **Note:** `console.log` exists but goes nowhere — the sandbox has no attached console. To see what a run did, return the values you care about; they're captured in the function's **Execution history**.
- [File Management](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/files.md): **Tip:** Use a logical folder structure that matches your projects or teams. For example: `/Marketing/2026/Q2` or `/Client Documents/Acme Corp`.
- [Getting Started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/getting-started.md): **Note:** Every workspace is fully isolated. Your data lives alongside other workspaces on the same platform, but security is enforced at the database row level — no other workspace can ever see or touch your data, and you can never see theirs.
- [Guest Users](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/guest-users.md): **Note:** Converted guest users are real accounts inside your organization, not separate organizations. They're simply flagged as guests, and the roles you assign determine what they can reach.
- [Connecting AI Apps via MCP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/mcp-connections.md): **Do not put tokens in the URL.** A `?jwt=…` query parameter lands in proxy and server logs and browser history. Portablemind now rejects ordinary session tokens passed that way; if your client cannot send an `Authorization` header, use OAuth (Option 1) instead.
- [Video Meetings (Meet)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/meet.md): **Tip:** if a teammate can't find Meet, check their security roles first — administrators grant **Meet (Video) Access** by assigning that security role to the person in the Administration area.
- [AI Memory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/memory.md): **Note:** Semantic search requires an embedding model to be configured for your workspace as part of [AI setup](ai-setup.md). Relationship classification can optionally use one of your configured chat models for higher accuracy.
- [Agent Orchestration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/orchestration.md): **Note:** Agents handle work *within* their stage. The engine handles flow *between* stages. Humans approve at gates. This separation exists because agents cannot reliably self-orchestrate handoffs — the engine keeps every run on rails.
- [Plans, Limits & Fair Use](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/plans-and-limits.md): **Tip:** if a fair-use guardrail is getting in your way during legitimate work, contact support. They can be raised — that's the point of calling them guardrails rather than plan limits.
- [Skills](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/skills.md): **Note:** Skills follow the **Agent Skills open standard** — the same `SKILL.md` format used by Claude Code, Codex, and the 1,000+ community skills. That means you can **import** skills from the ecosystem, and skills you build in Portablemind are portable. Learn about the standard at [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io).
- [Enterprise Sub-workspaces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/sub-workspaces.md): **Tip:** trying to put a sub-workspace on a plan above your contract tier is refused with a message saying so. Choose a lower plan, or talk to us about changing the tier.
- [Tickets, Partners & the Support Portal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/tickets-and-partners.md): **The AI difference is the one to weigh.** The Support Portal includes an AI agent that triages and answers tickets on its own. In a partnership, AI conversations stay inside the organization that owns them and are never shared across the partnership — so partners collaborate person-to-person on shared tickets. This is deliberate: an AI conversation carries context from its own organization, and sharing it could surface that organization's private data to the other side.
- [Connecting Google Vertex AI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/vertex-setup.md): **Note:** Vertex does not use API keys for Claude. Google's key-based "Express mode" covers only some Gemini use, and Anthropic's Claude models on Vertex require Google Cloud credentials. The connection below is what makes Claude on Vertex work.
- [Welcome to Portablemind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/welcome.md)
- [White-label Branding & Single Sign-on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/white-label.md): **Tip:** switching white-label off hides your branding and stops single sign-on, but keeps everything you configured. Switch it back on and it's all still there.
- [Workspace Sharing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/portablemind-ai/docs/main/guides/workspace-sharing.md): **Tip:** Revoking is permanent — it's a hard unshare, and re-establishing access afterwards requires a brand-new invitation.
